translation: The operations of angels are measured by discrete time.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch7, from Latin at farmer1998:12499

sources.text: Henry of Ghent, Quodlibet II, question 9
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit's identified source for the doctrine that angelic operations are measured by discrete time

doctrine: Farmer's note states that Pico discusses this issue in the Apologia (paraphrase, farmer1998:12578). Edelheit treats theses 6 and 7 together as angelology, reporting that thesis 6 holds that operations of angels are measured by definite time, with traces of the doctrine at Henry's Quodlibet II, question 9, a text he notes Pico knew well from the discussion of the Apology elsewhere in his book (paraphrase, edelheit2022:15499).
historiography: Edelheit's chapter is the only scholarship on this thesis found in the material consulted; he quotes the thesis's Latin verbatim from the printed 900 Theses, page 242 (edelheit2022:15521).

quotations.text: In thesis 6 we find that operations of angels are measured by definite time.

not_established: The content of Pico's discussion of this issue in the Apologia (Opera, 128), beyond Farmer's bare reference to it: not established by the sources consulted.
Reception of this thesis beyond Farmer's note and Edelheit's chapter: not established by the sources consulted.
